hidden.domain: A domain you may not see
hidden.platform: A platform you may not see
hidden.product: A product you may not see
hidden.contract: A contract you may not see

picker.nothing: No element of the catalogue matches
picker.more: The first {{shown}} of {{total}} matches – type more to narrow the search.

form.name: Name
form.keyHint: Lower case letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-” – used by the file format and as the ODPS id.
form.keyInvalid: Lower case letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”, starting with a letter or a digit
form.noDomain: No domain yet – the module's managers add them under Data → Domains
form.purposeHint: What the product is for and who it serves.
form.ownersHint: Users or teams who answer for the product. Named from outside its owning teams, they see and change it.
form.tierHint: 1 to 3: how the product is supported (hours, response).
form.versionHint: A label (ODPS version); the history is the audit trail.
form.valueHint: Shown beside the attributed costs – never set off against them.
form.externalRefsHint: A catalogue entry, a wiki page or a repository – Steward links out instead of copying.
form.refUrlInvalid: A web address that starts with http:// or https://

products.title: Data products
products.description: What the domains offer: products made of tables, topics, APIs and files, with their ports, owners, rating and health.
products.name: Name
products.noMatch: No data product matches the filters.
products.emptyText: A data product bundles what a domain offers – its tables, topics and APIs – with owners, ports, a rating and health.
products.costsIncomplete: Incomplete: a part you may not see is left out of the total.

product.deleteConfirm: Delete the data product “{{name}}” with its ports, bindings, consumers and memberships? The elements stay in the catalogue
product.noObjects: No data objects: name them on the output ports, or link the elements to the data objects they implement.
product.noOutputPorts: No output port yet – nothing to consume.

lifecycleForm.title: Lifecycle of {{name}}
lifecycleForm.sunsetHint: When the product (or port) is no longer offered. Consumers and the owners of consuming products are told.
lifecycleForm.confirm_one: {{count}} consumer still uses this product – retire it all the same
lifecycleForm.confirm_other: {{count}} consumers still use this product – retire it all the same
lifecycleForm.confirmRequired: Confirm that you retire the product while it is consumed
lifecycleForm.needsOwner: An active product needs a product owner.
lifecycleForm.needsOutputPort: An active product needs at least one output port.

hints.proposed: Proposed: an idea, not built yet.
hints.draft: Draft: being built; not offered to consumers yet.
hints.active: Active: offered to consumers. Needs a product owner and an output port.
hints.deprecated: Deprecated: still offered until the sunset date; consumers should move to the successor.
hints.retired: Retired: no longer offered. Consuming products show it on their input ports.

rating.title: CIA rating
rating.productHelp: Rate the product on the instance's CIA scale. Per dimension it should be at least as high as the data objects it exposes; lower is allowed with a reason (only aggregated data leaves the product).
rating.objectHelp: Rate the data object on the instance's CIA scale, with a justification per dimension – as applications are rated.
rating.highestClassification: Its data objects go up to {{value}}.
rating.floorHint: Its data objects need at least {{level}}.
rating.reasonLabel: Reason for being below its data objects
rating.reasonHint: E.g. only aggregated data leaves the product. With a reason the warning goes; without one the page, the list and the scorecard warn.
rating.belowExplained: Rated below its data objects, with a reason
rating.belowShort: Rated below its data objects without a reason

environments.title: Environments
environments.none: Not in any environment yet: bind a port or add elements, or add an environment here.
environments.removeConfirm: Remove {{environment}} from the product? Only an environment without bindings and elements can be removed

ports.help: Output ports are what the product offers, each optionally under a data contract; input ports say what it consumes. Per environment a binding names the elements a port exposes or reads.
ports.noOutputs: No output port yet: an active product needs one.
ports.noInputs: No input port: the product consumes nothing documented.
ports.deleteConfirm: Delete the port “{{name}}” with its bindings and registered consumers? Its elements stay members
ports.name: Name
ports.versionHint: E.g. v2 – a new version is a new port; deprecate the older one.
ports.fileFormatHint: What the port’s files are – discovery reads it from the bound files.
ports.partitioningHint: Partition keys in their order (dt, region) – Hive style key=value folders; Enter after each.
ports.deprecateNotice: Deprecating a port tells its registered consumers and the owners of products that consume it.
ports.apiRule: An API is an output port when a consumer uses it to read the domain's data for their own purpose; commands and workflows stay an application interface.
ports.objectsHint: Declared here; the objects its elements implement are added on their own.
ports.sourceRequired: Say where the data comes from

bindings.title: Port {{port}} in {{environment}}
bindings.removeConfirm: Remove the binding of “{{name}}” in {{environment}}? The elements stay members
bindings.elementsHint: Elements of {{environment}}, at most {{max}}. They become members of the product with the port's role.
bindings.contractHint: The ODCS contract the port is held to in this environment.
bindings.noContracts: No data contract you may see
bindings.versionHint: Empty: always the current one (now version {{n}}).
bindings.serverHint: The contract's server for this environment.

objectives.title: Objectives
objectives.hint: What consumers can expect: freshness and availability are evaluated from the linked checks.
objectives.bindingHint: Only what differs in this environment; empty fields keep the port's objectives.
objectives.freshnessHint: The data is at most this old.
objectives.availabilityHint: Share of time up or degraded over 30 days.
objectives.completenessHint: Share of the completeness tests (not null, row counts, volume) that passed over 30 days.

consumers.title: Consumers of {{name}}
consumers.derived_one: {{count}} product consumes this port through an input port.
consumers.derived_other: {{count}} products consume this port through their input ports.
consumers.agreementInvalid: Give the agreement's reference (a web address starts with http:// or https://)
consumers.contactsHint: Told when the port is deprecated.

steps.title: Steps
steps.help: How data moves: inputs → a runner → outputs. Documentation only – Steward runs nothing. A step is documented where its result lives.
steps.none: No steps yet: add one to draw how data moves through the product.
steps.name: Name
steps.inputsHint: Elements it reads – also of other products.
steps.outputsHint: Elements it writes: a step belongs with its outputs.
steps.hiddenInputs_one: And {{count}} input you may not see: it stays.
steps.hiddenInputs_other: And {{count}} inputs you may not see: they stay.
steps.runnerHidden: Its runner is something you may not see: choose one to replace it, or leave it empty to remove it.
steps.runnerYouMayNotSee: A runner you may not see
steps.runnerElementHint: A Snowflake task, a pipe or a dynamic table.

members.title: Elements of the product
members.elementsHint: Search the catalogue by name. Adding gives nobody rights on an element; one element can be part of several products.
members.roleHint: Input: consumed; internal: transformation and staging; output: offered. Binding to a port sets the role.
members.descendantsHint: A database, a schema or a topic bundle counts with its tables and topics – today's and future ones.
members.createdAndAdded: {{name}} added to the catalogue and to the product.
members.none: No elements yet: add tables, topics or APIs from the catalogue.
members.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}} from this product? It stays in the catalogue and in other products

health.help: Health comes only from checks linked to the elements or from the product's monitor – without them it says “No data”, never OK. Read from the stored check states: a page never calls a platform.

sources.elements: from its output elements (internal ones at most degrade it)

health.noDataHint: Create a monitor below, or link checks to the elements on their pages.
health.hasMonitor: The product has a monitor in this environment. “Update monitor” proposes checks for elements added since.
health.noMonitor: No monitor yet. “Create monitor” proposes one: a check per element along the pipeline, linked so that the root cause alerts.
health.monitorHint: You see the proposal first; the monitor is a disabled draft to review – Steward never enables it.
health.noElements: No output or internal elements in this environment.

monitor.createHelp: This draft monitor would watch the product. Review it, then apply: it is made disabled – enable it on its page once the maximum ages fit.
monitor.updateHelp: These checks would be added to the product's monitor for the elements added since; what is there stays as it is.
monitor.hidden: The product's monitor in this environment is one you may not see.
monitor.nothing: Nothing to add: every element is watched already, or none can be read.
monitor.links_one: {{count}} soft link along the steps: a stale upstream element is reported as the root cause.
monitor.links_other: {{count}} soft links along the steps: a stale upstream element is reported as the root cause.

skipReasons.unsupported_one: {{count}} element of a kind the check does not read
skipReasons.unsupported_other: {{count}} elements of a kind the check does not read
skipReasons.limit_one: {{count}} element beyond the limit of 100 checks
skipReasons.limit_other: {{count}} elements beyond the limit of 100 checks
skipReasons.noContractModule_one: {{count}} contract check left out: the data contracts module is off
skipReasons.noContractModule_other: {{count}} contract checks left out: the data contracts module is off

monitor.name: Name of the monitor
monitor.cannotApply: You may see the proposal, but not apply it: that needs the right to change the product and to create the monitor.
monitor.createdLong: The draft monitor “{{name}}” is made – disabled. Review its checks and maximum ages, then enable it.

costs.help: An attribution of the cost lines Steward reads – showback, never chargeback. Shared lines are split by the platform team's rule.
costs.title: Costs in {{month}}
costs.incomplete: Incomplete: part of the costs is on platforms whose amounts you may not see.
costs.showback: Showback: not booked and not part of a cost plan; the sum over products is not a budget.
costs.noEnvironment: The product is in no environment yet – its costs follow once it is.
costs.noMatches: No cost lines are matched to the product yet: add a match – a resource id, a sub-account, a service, a tag or an application.
costs.matchesHelp: Which cost lines are the product's: its own matches in this environment, and those of its elements (a topic's cluster, a connector).
costs.elementMatchesHelp: The products this element is part of take these lines in its environment.
costs.removeMatchConfirm: Remove the match {{match}}? Its lines are no longer attributed to the product
costs.matchFormHelp: Name the lines as the platform's bill carries them. A line two or more products match is shared and split by its allocation.

matchValueHints.resource: E.g. a Confluent cluster lkc-… or connector lcc-…, an AWS resource id.
matchValueHints.subAccount: E.g. a Snowflake account or a Confluent environment.
matchValueHints.service: The service name of the cost lines.
matchValueHints.application: The id of the application the lines are mapped to.

costs.matchHidden: A match on a platform you may not see

scorecard.title: Scorecard
scorecard.maturityHelp: Computed from the scorecard, never typed: 1 documented and rated, 2 observed, 3 contracted, 4 objectives met for 30 days, 5 endorsed.
scorecard.showNoEvidence_one: Show 1 more with no evidence yet
scorecard.showNoEvidence_other: Show {{count}} more with no evidence yet
scorecard.hideNoEvidence_one: Hide the one with no evidence yet
scorecard.hideNoEvidence_other: Hide the {{count}} with no evidence yet

evidence.noEvidenceYet: Steward has no evidence for this yet.

documented.has: {{done}} of {{of}}: description, owner, domain, type, data objects

rated.needsRerating: {{count}} to be rated again after a scale change
rated.belowFloor: Below its data objects without a reason: {{dimensions}}
rated.belowWithReason: {{count}} below its data objects, with a reason

contracted.withContract: {{count}} of {{of}} output ports under a contract

observed.withFreshness: {{count}} of {{of}} output elements have a freshness check

objectives.availabilityShort: Availability objective {{target}} %: the monitor has not run for 30 days yet
objectives.freshnessShort: {{port}}: freshness objective {{target}} %, no 30 days of checks yet
objectives.none: No objectives set on the output ports
objectives.completenessNoResults: {{port}}: completeness objective {{target}} %, no completeness results in 30 days

dependencies.ok: {{inputs}} input ports, none on a deprecated port
dependencies.deprecated: {{count}} of {{of}} input ports consume a deprecated or retired port

availability.noData: The monitor has no 30 days of samples yet

compliance.tests: Contract tests: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed, {{untested}} not tested

traceability.traced: {{count}} of {{of}} output elements traced to a source

understandability.defined: {{count}} of {{of}} exposed data objects have a definition

confidentiality.accessReviewed: An approved access review of its ports within 12 months.
confidentiality.notReviewed: No approved access review of its ports within 12 months.
confidentiality.personalFields_one: {{count}} personal field in the bound contracts
confidentiality.personalFields_other: {{count}} personal fields in the bound contracts
confidentiality.personalFieldsUndocumented_one: {{count}} personal field in the bound contracts, but no exposed data object holds personal data
confidentiality.personalFieldsUndocumented_other: {{count}} personal fields in the bound contracts, but no exposed data object holds personal data

quality.results: Tests: {{tests}} – {{passed}} passed, {{warning}} with a warning, {{failed}} failed (the latest of each, 30 days)

access.ownersHint: Responsibility, not a right of its own: named from outside the owning teams they see, change and manage the product – adding such an owner asks you to confirm it is you.

everyone.who: Every working role (products without owning teams)
everyone.what: See the product, its ports, elements and pipeline

designers.what: Create and change products; delete, owning teams and retiring

owners.what: See, change and manage their product

teams.what: Only members of those teams (with their roles), auditors and administrators

shares.what: View, Edit or Manage for a person, a team or a role – only for those who use the module; Restricted: only the shares, owners, auditors and administrators

access.scopeHint: What you may not see is neither listed nor counted nor named elsewhere – lineage and the map draw it without a name.

links.title: Links
links.helpProduct: Documents, change and incident records, ticket references and other entries that name this data product. Links are made on those entries.
links.helpObject: Documents, records, ticket references and other entries that name this data object. Links are made on those entries.

history.auditOnlyAuditors: Every change is in the audit log – auditors and administrators read it there.

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: The catalogue of tables, views, topics, APIs and file paths – discovered from the platforms or entered. One element can be part of several products.
elements.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}} from the catalogue? It leaves every product it is part of
elements.capped: More than {{count}} elements match: narrow the search.
elements.emptyText: Add a discovery source to read tables and topics from Snowflake, Kafka and database snapshots, or enter an element by hand.
elements.name: Name
elements.platformRequired: This kind lives on a platform – choose one
elements.noFittingPlatform: No platform you may see fits this kind
elements.missingNote: The last discovery runs did not find this element (since {{date}}). It stays while a product holds it; in no product it is removed after 30 days.
elements.typeLabelHint: E.g. Power BI dataset, Excel extract.

nameHints.snowflake: DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE – unquoted Snowflake names are upper case.
nameHints.kafka: The topic name, or the prefix of a bundle.
nameHints.api: A name for the API, e.g. shop-api.
nameHints.files: Bucket and prefix, or share and path.
nameHints.other: A name unique for its platform, kind and environment.

elements.apiHint: Name the operations that serve data (GET /customers); commands stay with the application.
elements.applicationHint: The application that owns the data (optional).
elements.discoveredHint: Discovered: its name, kind and environment come from the platform. You change the description, layer and links – a new read keeps them.
elements.noObjects: It implements no data object yet.
elements.noEditableObjects: No data object you may change
elements.readoutTruncated: A limit of the discovery run cut this read: the figures count a part of the objects.
elements.noReadout: Only discovered elements have a readout.
elements.draftHelp: Steward reads the element's columns or schema – metadata only – and drafts an ODCS contract. Review it; it becomes a contract only when you create it.

checks.title: Checks
checks.none: No check watches this element yet: link one, or create a monitor on its product.
checks.unlinkConfirm: Unlink this check from the element? The check itself stays
checks.hidden: A check you may not see
checks.help: Statuses are the stored ones – the page never reads the platform. Found checks name this element in their fields; link them to count them.

objects.title: Data objects
objects.description: What the business data is – customers, orders, measurements –, how sensitive it is and who answers for it: the business glossary of the data products.
objects.deleteConfirm: Delete the data object “{{name}}”? Products and elements lose the reference
objects.noMatch: No data object matches the filters.
objects.emptyText: A data object says what data is – a definition, a rating, a classification and whether it is personal data – and which elements implement it.
objects.classificationHint: Public, internal, confidential or strictly confidential – beside the CIA rating, not mapped onto it.
objects.retentionHint: An ISO 8601 duration such as P10Y, or text.
objects.flagsHint: Tags with a meaning – nothing is enforced.
objects.rolesHint: Responsibility, not rights: the data owner decides classification and access, stewards keep definitions and quality, custodians run where it is stored. Editing follows the owning teams.
objects.ownerUser: The data owner is a user
objects.custodiansHint: A team, or an application's responsible people.
objects.attributesHint: A light list, not a schema – the contract holds the fields.
objects.elementsHint: Link elements on their pages (Data objects it implements).
objects.products: Products that expose or process it

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: The business domains and their sub-domains (two levels) that products and data objects belong to, with owners and owning teams.
domains.deleteConfirm: Delete the domain “{{name}}”? Only a domain without sub-domains, products and data objects can be deleted
domains.emptyText: Domains group products and data objects: Sales, Customer, Manufacturing – with sub-domains such as Sales → Orders.
domains.whoCanAct: The module's managers (designers and administrators) add them.
domains.parentHint: Empty: a top-level domain. Sub-domains have no sub-domains of their own.
domains.parentLocked: It has sub-domains, so it stays a top-level domain.
domains.ownersHint: Users or teams who answer for the domain.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.description: Sources that read tables, views and topics from Snowflake, Kafka and database snapshots into the catalogue – metadata only, as the person who saved them.
discovery.deleteConfirm: Delete the discovery source “{{name}}”? The elements it found stay in the catalogue
discovery.emptyText: A source reads a platform's catalogue every day: databases and schemas on Snowflake, topics on Kafka, the schema snapshot of a database.
discovery.whoCanAct: The module's managers and the platform's managers set sources up.
discovery.formHelp: Steward reads metadata only – never data – with the platform's identity, as you: your right to use the platform is checked before every run.
discovery.platformHint: Snowflake, Kafka or a database platform you may use.
discovery.noPlatform: No platform you may use can be discovered

scopeHints.snowflake: Databases, or DATABASE.SCHEMA – Enter after each.
scopeHints.kafka: Topic prefixes; empty: every topic (internal ones left out).
scopeHints.database: Schema names; empty: the whole snapshot.
scopeHints.aws: S3 prefixes as s3://bucket/prefix/ – only these are listed (a bucket’s root only as s3://bucket/); empty: the files.path elements of products on this platform.

discovery.scopeSnowflakeRequired: Name at least one Snowflake database
discovery.includeHint: Only names starting with one of these – plain comparisons, no patterns.
discovery.excludeHint: Names starting with one of these are left out.
discovery.rulesHint: A database, schema or topic whose name starts or ends with a value belongs to an environment; the first match wins, else the platform's environment.
discovery.rulesIncomplete: Give each rule a value and an environment

modeHints.informationSchema: One database at a time, current, only what Steward's role has a privilege on.
modeHints.accountUsage: Every database in one statement, up to 90 minutes behind; the role needs IMPORTED PRIVILEGES and sees the whole account's metadata.

discovery.identityHint: Whom Steward reads as (not a privileged identity).
discovery.teams: Owning teams of what it finds
discovery.started: “{{name}}” is reading – the page shows the run when it ends
discovery.failingSince: Failing since {{date}} – the owner and the platform's managers were told once.
discovery.truncated: Stopped at a limit: nothing was marked missing.

settings.title: Data products
settings.help: The lists the data products module uses. Environments come from Settings → Environments, production first.
settings.layersHint: The pipeline draws elements in these columns; a layer typed on an element is kept as it is.
settings.flagsHint: Suggested on data objects; other flags can be typed.
settings.defaultsText: Discovery sources read every {{interval}} hours unless set otherwise; monitors and objectives are production's.

allocations.title: Shared lines
allocations.help: Lines several products match are split by their platform team's rule – equally, by weight or by measured use. Never more than 100 % of a line; what no product takes is not attributed.
allocations.over100: The weights add up to more than 100 %
allocations.hiddenKept_one: The weight of {{count}} product you may not see stays as it is.
allocations.hiddenKept_other: The weights of {{count}} products you may not see stay as they are.
allocations.audit: Who may manage the platform sets the split; it is in the audit log.

transfer.importIntro: Files of Steward's format – domains, data objects, elements and products, YAML or JSON – and ODPS v1 documents (Open Data Product Standard), read as products of the format. Check the preview first; nothing is written until you import.
transfer.filesHint: At most 500 files and 8 MB together.
transfer.tooLarge: The files are larger than 8 MB together.

modeHints.add: Entries that exist are left as they are.
modeHints.update: Entries that exist take what the files say; what a file leaves out keeps Steward's value. Nothing is removed.
modeHints.replace: As add and update, and the files are the whole of the earlier import of this origin: its entries the files no longer hold are removed, and the products' members, ports, steps and consumers the files leave out too. What you may not see is never removed.

transfer.jobElements: Importing in the background: {{done}} of {{total}} elements written
transfer.jobEntries: Writing the products, data objects and domains …
transfer.jobUndo: The import failed – taking back what it wrote …
transfer.jobFailed: The import failed – nothing of it was kept
transfer.jobUndone_one: {{count}} element it had added was removed again.
transfer.jobUndone_other: {{count}} elements it had added were removed again.
transfer.originHint: A name the import keeps its entries under (for example shop-catalogue) – an import that replaces it later names the same origin. Optional, except to replace.
transfer.originRequired: Replacing needs the origin of the earlier import.
transfer.doneReplace: Imported: {{add}} added, {{change}} changed, {{unchanged}} unchanged, {{remove}} removed, {{items}} list items removed
transfer.odpsRead_one: {{count}} ODPS document read as a data product.
transfer.odpsRead_other: {{count}} ODPS documents read as data products.
transfer.stepUp: The import removes more than one entry or list item: importing asks you to confirm it is you.
transfer.removeTitle: Remove what the files no longer hold?
transfer.removeItems_one: and {{count}} list item of entries that stay (members, ports, steps, consumers)
transfer.removeItems_other: and {{count}} list items of entries that stay (members, ports, steps, consumers)

measured.help: Each product takes its measured use of the line: credits of its warehouses or query tags, or the bytes written to its topics – priced with the platform’s contracted price book where it has a price, else as its share of everything measured. Read once a day; never more than the line together.

subjectsHint.confluentTopic: Its topics – none: its member topics

measured.hiddenKept_one: What is measured for {{count}} product you may not see stays as it is.
measured.hiddenKept_other: What is measured for {{count}} products you may not see stays as it is.
measured.notRead: Not read yet – the job reads it within the hour

pricing.book: priced with the platform’s price book
pricing.share: no price: share of the measured total

estimates.title: Estimated against attributed
estimates.help: Estimates made for this product (they belong to a service or a platform, under Costs) beside what is attributed to it. Showback: nothing is netted or booked.
estimates.none: No estimate is for this product yet – make one under Costs on a service or a platform and name this product as what it is for.

ossie.label: The data objects as an Apache Ossie model

trend.title: Maturity over time
trend.none: No daily snapshot yet – the first is taken within the next hour.
trend.caption: The maturity and the scorecard parts per day
trend.summary: Maturity from {{from}} to {{to}}: {{start}} at the start, {{now}} now

personal.title: Personal data in fields
personal.hint: Fields of the bound data contracts marked personal (customProperties personalData) or classified. The contract says it – Steward marks nothing itself.
personal.hidden_one: {{count}} bound contract you may not see
personal.hidden_other: {{count}} bound contracts you may not see

element.title: Quality
element.none: No quality results in the last 30 days. dbt tests, contract tests, Data Metric Functions and volume checks record them.
